**Synopsis:**
Treasury yields are rising in part because investors believe R-star (the neutral/natural rate of interest) is moving structurally higher, driven by AI-related capital expenditure from hyperscalers and surging U.S. government borrowing (national debt at $40T). The NY Fed's Laubach-Williams model puts R-star at 1.65% as of Q2 2026, but market participants believe the true level is higher. A higher R-star implies rates settle at structurally elevated levels across the curve, complicates Fed rate cuts, and is hitting the 30-year end hardest due to fiscal concerns and long-dated supply competition. Some analysts flag a possible long-term disinflationary flip from AI, but acknowledge it is too early to confirm any structural shift.

The article's closing emphasis is on the Fed being unable to easily cut, yields under renewed pressure this week, $40T national debt compounding supply dynamics, and R-star likely higher than the NY Fed model shows. Any dovish (disinflationary AI) offset is framed as speculative and long-dated. Net forward signal is higher-for-longer, bullish for yields, bearish for duration.
